We investigate a random grain model where the number of grains within a given space is determined by a Poisson process with a variable intensity, and each grain's size is drawn from a distribution with a heavy-tailed distribution. The exponent of this heavy-tailed distribution varies with the intensity, and we examine the asymptotic behavior of the total volume of grains as the intensity approaches infinity. Our findings indicate that the total volume, when scaled appropriately, converges to a compound Poisson process, and we demonstrate the validity of a functional central limit theorem for the total volume in the case of independent intensities.

Emerging Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) are poised to play a significant role in the development of future 6G wireless networks. These RISs can be used to create a virtual aerial network, which is crucial for providing high-speed connectivity in remote areas. This paper investigates the potential of a hybrid RIS-UAV system, which combines RISs with a UAV to offer seamless connectivity to users. To optimize the system's performance, we develop a joint optimization framework that considers the UAV's location, RIS phase shifts, and transmission power. To overcome the complexity of this optimization problem, we introduce an efficient solution using a combination of Dinkelbach's algorithm and Successive Convex Approximation. Our simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in improving the system's performance.

This research focuses on optimizing the efficiency of complex, interconnected systems that involve numerous agents, where each agent's behavior is influenced by a specific objective function. To address the challenge of analyzing the performance of these systems, a novel approach is introduced, combining elements of optimal control and large deviation theory. By using this method, it is possible to identify the most effective control strategies for complex systems, even when the individual agents' behaviors are uncertain. A key advantage of this approach is that it allows for the derivation of analytical solutions to complex stochastic problems, which can be used to inform the design of more efficient control systems.

This paper presents a novel approach to training deep neural networks with minimal bit quantization, specifically reducing the computational complexity of convolutional neural networks. We introduce a technique that enables the training of binary weights and activation maps using gradient descent, and demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving high accuracy with minimal computational resources. We also propose a method for optimizing binary convolutional layers, and show that it can significantly improve the performance of binary neural networks. Furthermore, we propose a novel approach to training binary neural networks that leverages the power of gradient descent to achieve high accuracy with minimal bit quantization. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method by achieving high accuracy on multiple benchmark datasets, and show that it can outperform existing methods with minimal bit quantization.

A Type Ia supernova is a cataclysmic event that occurs when a white dwarf star reaches a critical mass, triggering an explosive nuclear reaction. This event can be triggered by a merger of two white dwarfs, a mass transfer from a companion star, or a collision between the two stars. Researchers have recently discovered a Type Ia supernova, named iPTF16gql, which shares characteristics with a merger of two white dwarfs. This discovery has led to a hypothesis that the supernova may have been caused by a merger of two white dwarfs, which would explain the supernova's unusual properties.

In this research, we investigate the online learning of complex, non-linear systems with adaptive computation allocation. We develop a theoretical framework for resource distribution based on the current level of estimation accuracy, and demonstrate its practical value in real-world applications, such as image and video processing, where our approach yields improved results compared to traditional methods.

The COVID-19 pandemic has severely impacted the global economy and has led to significant disruptions in the healthcare sector. In response, the world has been working to control the virus through widespread testing and vaccination programs. However, the current testing and vaccination processes are plagued by inefficiencies, including the need for manual verification of test results and vaccination records, which can lead to delays and inaccuracies. To address these challenges, a blockchain-based solution has been proposed, which aims to streamline the testing and vaccination processes by providing a secure, transparent, and efficient platform for the verification of test results and vaccination records. The solution leverages the capabilities of blockchain technology to enable the secure storage and verification of data, while also facilitating the integration of real-time data and facilitating the integration of real-time data. The proposed solution is designed to be a comprehensive solution for the testing and vaccination processes, which can be used to facilitate the integration of real-time data and facilitate the integration of real-time data.

Recent pre-trained language models have achieved top performance in numerous NLP tasks, including text classification. However, the lack of standard evaluation metrics and data makes it challenging to compare the effectiveness of these models. To address this issue, we introduce a comprehensive evaluation framework for comparing sentence embedding models in text classification. Our framework involves testing 15 sentence embedding models on 11 datasets, and we provide a detailed analysis of their performance using multiple evaluation metrics. The results show that using pre-trained models as sentence embeddings significantly outperforms traditional methods, and we offer insights into the factors that influence their performance. Our study also highlights the importance of choosing the right evaluation metrics and data for comparing sentence embedding models.

We investigate the behavior of a quantum particle in a $d$-dimensional lattice, where the presence of a magnetic field and the preservation of time reversal symmetry are considered. The system's behavior is analyzed using a specific model, where the particle's diffusion properties are studied in the context of the Anderson model. The results show that the diffusion rate is influenced by the breakdown of the particle-hole symmetry, leading to a faster diffusion rate. The study also examines the behavior of the system at different levels of disorder, revealing that the particle's behavior is characterized by a specific scaling law. The analysis is based on the use of the self-consistent Born approximation, which is used to study the system's behavior in the presence of strong disorder. The results of the study are compared to the predictions of the diffusion model, which is used to describe the behavior of the system in the context of the Anderson model.

Theoretical analysis of the Kerr precession in a quantum Hall ferromagnet has been conducted, revealing that the primary mechanism of attenuation is due to the non-conservation of angular momentum. This occurs when the angular momentum of a spin wave is transferred to the orbital motion of electrons, conserving total momentum. The study found that the Kerr precession's quality factor is directly related to the spin-orbit interaction strength, exhibiting a unique dependence on the excitation frequency. This correlation is in agreement with experimental findings, suggesting that the spin-orbit interaction is responsible for attenuation.

We investigate the behavior of a driven conformal field theory with time-varying space-dependent forces, and find that it undergoes a phase transition from a thermal state to a novel phase called the holographic phase. This phase is marked by the emergence of a characteristic length scale, which arises from a dimensional shift in the dual holographic theory. We examine the properties of the holographic phase, including its temperature, particle density, and entanglement entropy, and discover that it exhibits unique scaling properties. We also study the effects of driving on the thermalization of local operators and the growth of operator matrix elements, and find that they exhibit distinct behaviors in the thermal and holographic phases. Our findings provide a deeper understanding of the effects of time-periodic driving in quantum systems.

This research introduces a novel generative model that integrates multiple sensor inputs to enhance the performance of sensor fusion applications. The model is designed to generate data from various sensor modalities simultaneously, thereby enabling the creation of synthetic datasets that can be used to train robust models. To achieve this, the model employs a shared latent space that is shared across all sensor modalities, allowing it to generate data from different sources in a coordinated manner. The model's effectiveness is demonstrated through its successful application in generating synthetic data for a 3D object detection task, where it outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.

A recent analysis of $B^0$ decays into $K^+K^-$ and $K^0_S K^0_S$ final states has been conducted using data collected by the LHCb experiment at various collision energies. The measured $C\!P$-violating phases in these decays are found to be $\phi_{\rm sl}^{K^+K^-} = (170.7 \pm 3.0^\circ)$ and $\phi_{\rm sl}^{K^0_S K^0_S} = (170.3 \pm 2.8^\circ)$, which are consistent with the expected value of the $B_d$ mixing angle. The measured $B^0$ mixing frequencies are $\Delta m_d = 758.3 \pm 0.4 \text{~fs}$ and $\Delta m_d = 758.0 \pm 0.4 \text{~fs}$ for the two decay channels, respectively. The measured $B^0$ and $B^0_s$ mixing frequencies show agreement with the Standard Model predictions.

This research focuses on developing distributed optimal control strategies for Graph Symmetric Systems, which are a type of multi-agent system with symmetries in their structure and objectives. GSSs are characterized by a network symmetry and shared goals that are invariant under the symmetry. The study derives conditions that allow for the design of distributed optimal control strategies that achieve the same results as centralized controllers, without requiring full knowledge of the entire system. The proposed conditions rely on the properties of the symmetry group and the system's structure, and they enable the design of controllers that can be implemented in a distributed manner. The results of this research are applied to a specific type of GSS called identical multi-agent systems, which are a special case where the symmetry group is a permutation group. The study also includes numerical examples that illustrate the design of distributed optimal control strategies for GSSs, and it shows that these strategies can achieve the same results as centralized controllers, without requiring full knowledge of the entire system.

This study focuses on reducing the complexity of a labeled random finite set filter, particularly in the context of a labeled multi-Bernoulli (LMB) filter. A new method is introduced to truncate the LMB state distribution, yielding a truncated labeled multi-Bernoulli (LMB-T) filter. By analyzing the posterior mean, it is shown that the new method effectively controls the expected number of targets. A comparative analysis of a conventional method and the new method reveals that the new method offers a more favorable trade-off between target accuracy and computational complexity.

Research into typological databases has been hindered by the scarcity of reliable data.  One method to address this issue is by utilizing unsupervised knowledge base completion techniques that can infer missing information from existing databases.  This paper presents a new approach to completing the Universal Language Tree by utilizing a graph neural network to predict missing language relationships.  Our model outperforms existing benchmarks, and the enhanced tree is made available for further use.

In reinforcement learning, evaluating a policy's performance is crucial, particularly when the ideal data is unavailable.  Off-policy evaluation addresses this challenge by estimating the policy's performance using historical data collected from a different policy.  A significant hurdle in achieving accurate results is the high variance associated with the commonly used inverse propensity score method.  To mitigate this issue, we introduce a novel approach that leverages the relationship between the target and reference policies.  By doing so, our method can effectively handle situations where the target policy is not explicitly known.  We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through both theoretical analysis and experimental validation.

The production of biophoraceuticals is a complex process that requires precise control to ensure the desired outcome. To achieve this, a data-driven approach is used to develop a predictive model that can forecast the product quality based on the process conditions. This model is then integrated into a control system that can adjust the process parameters to optimize the product quality. However, the model itself can introduce errors, which can significantly impact the final product quality. To address this issue, a new method is proposed that can accurately predict the final product quality by accounting for the model risk. This method uses a data-driven approach to estimate the model risk and then uses this information to make more accurate predictions. The proposed method is tested using a real-world dataset and shown to outperform traditional methods in terms of prediction accuracy.

We have developed a new approach to study the properties of a large polaron in a 3D environment with a Fröhlich interaction. By combining the Fröhlich coupling with the bare electron's kinetic energy, we've created a framework that allows us to derive an effective Hamiltonian for the electron. By using a variational method, we've been able to calculate the energy-momentum relation for the polaron and its corresponding binding energy. Our results show that the polaron's energy-momentum relation is consistent with the standard form, and we've found that the polaron's binding energy is dependent on the momentum. We've also shown that the polaron's binding energy is consistent with the standard expression for a polaron at rest. Our results have implications for the study of polarons in superconductors and other systems.

We investigate the electric field operator's lifetime in a magnetized vacuum, where the Landau quantization of the electron's motion influences its temporal characteristics. By applying a perturbative approach to the vacuum's one-loop effective action, we determine the electric field operator's two-point correlation function and the lifetime of its excited states. Our results show that strong magnetic fields can significantly extend the lifetime of the electric field operator, with the lifetime's dependence on the magnetic field strength and its orientation.

The quantum principle of complementarity indicates that certain properties of a quantum system cannot be defined together. This study explores the possibility of describing the same system with multiple representations, or 'pictures', simultaneously. By demonstrating that the principle of complementarity is weaker than the possibility of switching between these representations, we establish that the representations are not truly complementary. This implies that a system can be described with multiple representations at once, or that we can choose which representation to use based on the specific property we want to define. This finding has implications for the development of quantum information technology, as it suggests that a quantum system can be described using multiple representations to facilitate the processing of information.

We have developed a mathematical framework to examine the properties of periodic arrangements, focusing on the presence of non-expansive lines and the application of the Herman-Minkowski theorem. This framework enables us to determine the set of all possible periodic configurations for a given sequence of integers, and it forms the basis for our investigation into the properties of aperiodic and uniquely winoic configurations, particularly in the context of the unique tilting theorem.

Recent advances in NLP have been largely driven by the availability of vast, high-quality datasets. However, for languages with limited resources, collecting such data is often impractical. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach to training virtual assistants in under-resourced languages by utilizing a multilingual model that has been pre-trained on high-resource languages. Our method involves using a multilingual BERT model to generate responses in low-resource languages, and we evaluate its performance on a dataset of 1,000 dialogues in Swahili. Our results show that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving a 20% improvement in response quality.

quasi-exactly solvable states in the relative coordinate, using a specific 
exponential form to describe the potential. We then apply this method to 
several well-known exactly solvable potentials, such as the harmonic oscillator, 
and the Caldeira-Lanczos model, to illustrate its effectiveness.

Convolutional neural networks have been extensively used in computer vision tasks, yet their performance is often limited by the input resolution, which is typically set at 224x224 pixels. This restriction is largely due to the computational costs associated with higher resolutions. To overcome this issue, we introduce a novel architecture called Convolutional Neural Network with Adaptive Resolution (CARLA), which dynamically adjusts the input resolution for each layer based on the size of the convolutional kernels. By doing so, CARLA effectively reduces the computational burden while maintaining the accuracy of traditional CNNs. In our experiments, CARLA demonstrates comparable performance to ResNet-50 and ResNet-101 on the ImageNet-1K benchmark, despite a significant reduction in computational costs.

We investigate the impact of spin state excitation on the surface of binary asteroids, focusing on the case of satellite (2000 DO) with its primary asteroid, 2015 TO7. The satellite's spin state excitation can occur due to the YORP effect, leading to a rapid rotation period of around 10 minutes. The spin state excitation can cause the surface of the satellite to be restructured due to the stress on its material, resulting in a change in the albedo of the surface. The albedo change can be significant, leading to variations in the satellite's brightness. The satellite's rotation period can also change due to the spin state excitation, leading to a change in the satellite's brightness. The satellite's rotation period can be measured by observing its brightness over time, which can be used to determine the satellite's spin state. The satellite's spin state can also be used to determine the satellite's mass and density.

A numerical method is developed to solve the Einstein-Maxwell-scalar field equations in the context of an asymptotically flat, stationary black hole with distinct charges. The approach involves a scalar field evolution equation and metric equation expressed in a specific coordinate system, with the boundary conditions tailored to accommodate the event horizon and spatial infinity. The method is tested by simulating the collapse of a charged black hole with a square profile scalar field, and the results are verified through the conservation of energy and momentum. The study also examines the behavior of scalar field perturbations and the stability of the final equilibrium state.

The sensitivity of the C\o{S}TANTS experiment to sterile neutrino decays is examined, particularly in the context of the relationship between active and sterile neutrinos. The analysis considers the decay of a sterile neutrino into an active neutrino and a dark photon, which is then converted into an electron-positron pair. The experiment's sensitivity is found to be significantly influenced by the mixing angle and the mass of the sterile neutrino, with the most pronounced effects occurring in the 100-200 MeV mass range. The C\o{S}TANTS experiment is shown to be capable of probing the mixing angle of sterile neutrinos down to 10^-3 for masses in the 10-100 MeV range, with the potential to improve upon existing constraints.

Recent breakthroughs in image denoising have been driven by deep learning techniques, particularly those that leverage self-supervised learning. A widely used approach involves training a denoising autoencoder on a large dataset of natural images without any paired images with known noise levels. However, the effectiveness of these self-supervised methods heavily relies on the quality of the training data, which can be compromised by the presence of artifacts in the training images. To address this issue, we propose a novel self-supervised denoising autoencoder that can effectively remove artifacts from the training images. Our proposed method employs a denoising autoencoder to generate a noise-free version of the training images, which are then used to train a second self-supervised denoising autoencoder. Our proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art self-supervised denoising techniques in terms of both objective and subjective evaluations.

The goal of k-sparse recovery is to identify a k-sparse vector x from the given measurement matrix Ax, where A has m rows and n columns. A novel algorithm is introduced that uses a novel sampling strategy to efficiently retrieve x from Ax, achieving optimal sample complexity with high probability. This algorithm is specifically designed to handle the case where the matrix A is a Gaussian random matrix, and it is shown to achieve the optimal sample complexity of O(k log (n/k)) with high probability.

Union and intersection types in gradually typed languages such as TypeScript enable the creation of complex type expressions. However, the verification of these types poses a challenge due to their non-standard characteristics. This research focuses on the problem of verifying union and intersection types in a gradual setting. We present a method to address this issue by utilizing the type system's own gradual annotation, which allows us to disregard the specific union and intersection operators. Our approach is demonstrated to be equivalent to the original type system, which we prove through the use of a gradual logical relation.

Reinforcement learning offers a framework for developing goal-oriented motor learning skills, which can be applied to both biological and artificial systems. End-effect drives, which are crucial for motor learning, have been extensively used in robotics and are also a vital component of biological motor systems. This study introduces a novel reinforcement learning method called goal-based end-effect drives, which can be used in both biological and artificial systems. The proposed approach is tested using a simulated brain model and a robotic arm, which demonstrates its ability to learn and adapt to new goals. Furthermore, this method is shown to be more efficient than traditional methods in terms of learning speed and accuracy.

The anharmonicity of a potential, which deviates from a perfectly harmonic potential, has significant implications for the thermodynamic properties of systems. In an ideal gas, the incorporation of anharmonicity leads to notable changes in the heat capacity, while in contrast, the application of the central limit theorem to anharmonic potentials results in the convergence of their probability density functions towards a Gaussian distribution.

In Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity, we investigate the correlation functions of scalar field operators at late times, and our analysis reveals a non-zero constant that emerges from a specific spacetime component. Furthermore, we examine the implications of this constant on the system's operator algebra, and we also consider the connection between the system's Hamiltonian and the system's age.

Social media platforms like Twitter have become a primary source of information for individuals, but they are also vulnerable to the spread of misinformation and disinformation. Twitter's policies prohibit users from sharing content that promotes hate speech, disinformation, and other forms of misconduct. When users violate these policies, they may face temporary or permanent suspension. This study focuses on a subset of suspended Twitter users who were involved in discussions surrounding the 2020 US presidential election. By analyzing their tweets, we identified patterns of language and behavior that were associated with a higher likelihood of suspension, including the use of offensive and disinformation. Our research also revealed that certain groups of users were more likely to be suspended, including those who were more politically active and engaged in discussions about the election.

This report outlines the physics potential of the 120 TeD proton-ion collider, a proposed high-energy facility. It covers electron hadron scattering, high-energy electron production via deep inelastic scattering, and related topics including electroweak particle research, hadron structure, and exotic particle searches.

Creating accurate, comprehensive labels for large datasets of images sourced from crowds is a complex task due to the inherent noise and diversity in annotations. To address this challenge, we propose an innovative approach that utilizes a combination of visual and textual information to automatically generate labels. This method involves a multi-stage process: first, it uses a deep learning model to identify objects in images, then it leverages a specialized network to refine these predictions based on visual features, and finally, it incorporates semantic relationships between objects to produce accurate labels. By incorporating both visual and textual data, our approach is able to generate precise labels for a diverse set of images, even in the presence of noise and diverse annotations.

The 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) has developed a cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) standard, which enables direct communication between devices without needing a base station. C-V2X utilizes a resource allocation strategy that allows devices to randomly select and allocate resources for transmission. However, this approach can lead to collisions and packet loss, which can be mitigated by considering the devices' channel state information. This paper proposes a new C-V2X resource allocation method that utilizes real-time channel state information to minimize collisions and packet loss. The proposed method's performance is evaluated using a simulation model, which demonstrates its effectiveness in reducing collisions and improving throughput compared to the baseline C-V2X standard.

Deep neural network models have achieved remarkable success in various AI domains, but their lack of interpretability poses a significant challenge. To address this issue, researchers have developed methods to analyze the behavior of these models, but these approaches often rely on the assumption that the models are fixed. In reality, however, models are frequently updated to improve their performance, which raises concerns about how these updates affect their interpretability. To address this gap, we introduce a novel framework that assesses the stability of a model's explanations over time. Our framework is designed to provide a more comprehensive understanding of a model's behavior, taking into account the dynamic nature of its updates. To validate the effectiveness of our framework, we conducted experiments on a real-world dataset and compared the results with those of a baseline model. Our findings suggest that the proposed framework provides valuable insights into the behavior of deep neural network models, particularly in terms of their robustness to updates. Overall, our framework offers a new perspective on the interpretability of deep learning models and paves the way for future research in this area.

In collaborative software development, multiple contributors often work on the same codebase, necessitating the execution of specific tests to validate the work. However, the sheer number of potential test combinations can be overwhelming, and running all tests can be impractical. To address this issue, developers frequently disable certain tests, known as feature toggles, to expedite the testing process. However, this approach can lead to a significant risk of overlooking critical test cases. To address this issue, we propose a method for identifying test cases that are disabled due to feature toggles, and we evaluate the effectiveness of this approach through a case study involving 10 developers. Our results demonstrate that our method can identify a substantial number of disabled test cases, and we provide recommendations for mitigating the associated risks.

In the context of a 2+1 dimensional, rotating fluid with an enstrophy current, we investigate how energy and enstrophy propagate through the system. Utilizing a two-dimensional rotating fluid model, we develop a method to measure energy and enstrophy transport, and apply it to a rotating Bose-Einstein condensate. Our results show that energy flows outward while enstrophy flows inwards, and we find that enstrophy transport is significantly stronger than energy transport. Furthermore, we discover that the enstrophy current is influenced by the strength of the system's rotation.

This paper presents a groundbreaking network design for processing large-scale point clouds, which is often too extensive to analyze in its entirety. Our approach involves a novel architecture that divides the point cloud into multiple segments, classifies each segment, and then integrates these classifications to produce a comprehensive classification of the entire point cloud. Our method is tested on a large-scale point cloud dataset, and its performance is compared to existing techniques, demonstrating its effectiveness.

A measurement of the muon magnetic dipole moment has been conducted using the Muon g-2 experiment at Fermilab, yielding a value of $a_\mu = (28.52 \pm 0.15) \times 10^{-6}$. This result is in line with the Standard Model's prediction and is also consistent with the previous measurement from the Brookhaven E821 experiment.

The article examines the impact of domestic constraints on a state's ability to negotiate peaceful resolutions with adversaries. By applying a game-theoretic model, it explores how domestic constraints affect a state's capacity to make credible commitments to its adversaries. The results show that domestic constraints can either facilitate or hinder peaceful coexistence, depending on the nature of the constraints. The analysis considers the influence of public opinion, international norms, and domestic politics on a state's ability to make credible commitments. The article also investigates the role of international institutions in facilitating peaceful resolution and discusses the implications of these findings for international relations theory.

The brain's neural patterns are capable of encoding complex linguistic structures,
but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We hypothesize that neural patterns
represent the brain's internal model of the world, which is constructed from the
fundamental components of language. This internal model is shaped by the brain's
interpretation of the world, and it is this interpretation that is encoded in the
brain's internal language. This internal language is then used to generate
neural patterns, which are the brain's way of communicating with the rest of the
body. This internal model is constantly updated and refined as new information is
received, and it is this dynamic process that gives rise to the brain's ability to
produce complex linguistic patterns.

The IceCube Neutrino Observatory has identified 13 high-energy neutrinos linked to the blazar TXS 0506+056, which exhibited a significant high-energy emission in 2015. These detected neutrinos were found to coincide temporally with the blazar's emission, which began 159 days after its outburst. The analysis involved a sophisticated method to account for background events, which were found to be consistent with the predicted rates. The significance of these detected neutrinos was found to be 4.8 standard deviations, indicating a statistically significant correlation. The study also considered alternative explanations, such as a possible connection to a gamma-ray burst, which was found to be unlikely. The study's findings support the hypothesis that TXS 0506+006 is the source of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos.

A newly developed adaptive optics system, the MMT-GEM, has been designed to achieve optimal performance by utilizing a secondary mirror that is cooled to match the ambient temperature. This minimizes the impact of thermal fluctuations on the wavefront, resulting in improved image quality. Our research focuses on the GEM's performance in the K-band using the MMT-11m telescope, specifically examining the effects of the secondary mirror's temperature on the wavefront and image quality. Our findings indicate that the GEM's performance is highly sensitive to temperature variations, with a 0.1 K temperature difference causing a significant degradation in image quality. To mitigate this issue, we have implemented a temperature control system that maintains the secondary mirror's temperature within 0.05 K of the ambient temperature, resulting in a significant improvement in image quality. Our results demonstrate that the GEM's performance is significantly enhanced by this temperature control system, achieving a Strehl ratio of 0.55 and a FWHM of 0.07 arcsec.

Accurate first principles predictions of lattice dynamics are essential for making reliable predictions of materials' properties. However, the current methods for calculating phonon spectra are often inaccurate or unreliable. This paper presents a novel approach to calculating the phonon spectrum of a material by combining the supercell method and the density functional perturbation theory. The method is validated by comparing its results with those of the supercell method for a set of materials, including a perovskite, a transition metal dichalcogenide, and a two-dimensional material. The method is then applied to a set of materials, including a set of perovskites, a set of transition metal dichalcogenides, and a set of two-dimensional materials, to calculate their phonon spectra. The method is found to be accurate and efficient, and is shown to be capable of predicting the phonon spectrum of a material with a high degree of accuracy. We introduce a new approach to verifying termination in the context of very-WSTS, expanding upon the widely used backward procedure. This novel verification condition is formulated as a first-order formula, incorporating constraints on acceleration levels - the maximum number of consecutive acceleration steps since the procedure's initiation. This innovation enables the utilization of well-established termination analysis techniques, such as the Karp-Miller algorithm with acceleration capping, to validate termination. We demonstrate the practical value of this method by applying it to the termination proofs of several well-known timed systems.

The James Webb Space Telescope's groundbreaking discoveries are contingent on the effective use of its high-resolution images. A new deep learning-based method has been developed to enhance the quality of astronomical images captured by the JWST. This approach utilizes a dual-branch neural network, combining a denoising autoencoder and a generative adversarial network to remove noise and improve image quality. The method's efficacy has been demonstrated through its application to JWST images of the Carina Nebula, resulting in clearer, higher-quality images. The technique's potential for JWST data analysis is promising, and it may be applied to other astronomical datasets as well.

A fundamental question in decoherence theory revolves around the emergence of classical behavior in quantum systems.  This inquiry is particularly pressing in the context of black hole physics, where the black hole information paradox necessitates an explanation for the emergence of classical behavior in black holes.  This paper examines the extent to which the conventional decoherence framework can provide such an explanation.  It is argued that the conventional framework falls short in addressing this issue, and that a revised approach is required.  This proposed framework posits that the emergence of classical behavior in black holes is a result of the interplay between the black hole's environment and its internal degrees of freedom.  This proposed framework is then shown to be consistent with the principles of the black hole information paradox.

This paper presents a method for determining the boundary of the geometric sum of ellipsoids in parametric form. Unlike existing approaches that rely on iterative techniques, such as the ellipsoid algorithm, our approach yields a direct formula. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the boundary of the sum can be represented using a rational function, with the coefficients of this function calculated through a straightforward formula.

Recent studies have shown that deep learning techniques excel in image and text processing, but their effectiveness in handling tabular data remains a topic of debate. A thorough analysis of 17 prominent datasets across 102 models has revealed that hybrid deep learning methods consistently outperform traditional methods, particularly in scenarios with limited data. This research has also provided valuable insights into the factors influencing model performance, including the number of training samples, the number of features, and the number of classes.

In the context of machine learning for radio frequency (RF) signals, transfer learning has emerged as a promising approach to enhance model performance. However, the effectiveness of transfer learning in RF applications heavily relies on the similarity between the source and target domains. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a novel method for quantifying RF signal similarity using a combination of statistical and spectral features. A statistical feature is derived from the probability density function of the signal, while spectral features are obtained from the power spectrum and its statistical properties. A comparison of these features with existing methods reveals that the proposed approach yields more accurate results, particularly for RF signals with different parameters.

The center vortex model is a theoretical framework used to explain how confinement occurs in quantum chromodynamics. It is also a useful tool for simulating QCD in a lower-dimensional setting, specifically in a 1+3 dimensional gauge theory. This lower-dimensional theory shares some characteristics with QCD, such as the presence of a massless particle, but it also has a massive particle that is related to confinement. By using center vortex configurations in this gauge theory, researchers have been able to study the properties of hadrons, such as their masses and decay patterns. This work examines the effectiveness of the center vortex model in reproducing experimental data on the properties of mesons, including their masses and decay patterns, and compares the results with actual measurements.

We have used the Fermi-LAT 12-year dataset to search for dark matter annihilations in 24 nearby dwarf galaxies, employing a novel method that accounts for the effects of baryons on the dark matter distribution. By combining this approach with a previously developed likelihood analysis, we have been able to significantly constrain the annihilation rate of dark matter particles, particularly when considering the effects of baryons. Our results show that, for the case of annihilation into $\tau^+ \tau^-$, the 95% confidence upper limit on the cross-section is $1.44 \times 10^{-26}$ cm$^3$/s, which is a factor of 1.5-2.5 tighter than previous limits. Furthermore, we have found that the inclusion of baryons in our analysis is crucial for obtaining these constraints. Our analysis also reveals that, for other channels, the constraints are less stringent, but we have found that the constraints are strongest when assuming a baryon-enhanced dark matter distribution.

In software development, change requests are crucial for understanding a project's functionality, but selecting relevant search terms from them can be a time-consuming task. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel approach that utilizes a pre-trained language model to extract key terms from change requests, leveraging the model's ability to identify relevant information. Our method was tested on a large dataset of 1,000 change requests from the Eclipse project, and the results show that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in extracting important terms.

This study introduces a novel, adaptive numerical method for solving complex systems of Darcy equations that account for multiple interacting fluid compartments within porous media. By incorporating a cell-based metric tensor, the approach effectively manages the distinct properties of each fluid, enabling a more accurate representation of their interactions. A comprehensive analysis of this method's stability and adaptability is presented, with a focus on its ability to handle various fluid configurations and material properties. Furthermore, this method is demonstrated through numerical simulations of 2D and 3D systems, showcasing its effectiveness in modeling systems with multiple fluid phases and spatially varying characteristics.

The development of dialogue summarization has been hindered by the inherent complexities of conversations, specifically their non-linear structure and the presence of diverse viewpoints. To address this issue, we have created a new dataset that utilizes multi-faceted annotations to capture the nuanced aspects of conversation topics. Our approach involves analyzing the relationship between these annotated topics and the summarization process, ultimately leading to the creation of an innovative system that generates both structured and unstructured summaries. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in accurately capturing the main points of a conversation, while also providing additional insights into the content.

The thermal movement of target nuclei causes Doppler broadening, which affects how neutrons interact with them.  In the case of neutron-nucleus interactions, this broadening has a significant impact on how neutrons are scattered elastically.  To better understand this effect, we've developed a new method to calculate the broadening cross-section, which is based on the convolution of impulse approximation and a Gaussian distribution.  This approach is then used to calculate cross-sections for elastic scattering of neutrons on hydrogen, carbon, and iron, and the results are compared to those from a semi-empirical model and existing data.  The newly proposed model provides a more accurate description of elastic scattering cross-sections at higher temperatures than previous methods.

This paper introduces the concept of n-Lie algebras within the context of Poisson manifolds and establishes a framework for n-Lie algebras. It further develops the notion of n-Pre-Lie algebras and demonstrates how these structures can be used to construct phase spaces. Additionally, the paper explores the relationship between N-graded Lie algebras and N-Pre-Lie algebras.

This research aims to maximize the rate of non-real-time users within a cell-free massive MIMO system, subject to constraints on time-sensitive data transmission, network capacity, and total power consumption. To achieve this, we propose a novel framework that integrates machine learning and optimization techniques. Our approach involves using a deep neural network to forecast the quality of signal connections and combining this with a reinforcement learning algorithm to adaptively adjust power levels. Simulation results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing systems in terms of overall efficiency and fairness.

We examine the norm of approximating an entire function $f$ using translations $f(\cdot + \xi_k)$ for a given sequence $\xi_k$. This investigation leads to characterizations of entire functions that can be accurately approximated to an extent that excludes functions of a certain growth class.

We have developed a theoretical framework that explains the thermodynamic principles governing energy dissipation in densely packed colloidal systems. This framework is built upon a microscopic understanding of how particles interact with their surrounding environment, and it provides a detailed explanation of how energy is dissipated in response to changes in the system's structure. Our theory is based on a fundamental principle of thermodynamics, and it accurately predicts the amount of energy dissipated in response to changes in the system's structure. We have tested our theory using computer simulations of colloidal systems, and our results show that the theoretical predictions match the computer simulations with a high degree of accuracy. Our theory also provides a detailed explanation of how energy is dissipated in response to changes in the system's structure, and it can be used to predict the behavior of densely packed colloidal systems under various conditions.

Continual object detection poses a more complex challenge than traditional incremental classification tasks. This is largely due to the need to effectively manage the coexistence of old and newly introduced object categories, as well as the need to maintain the spatial relationships between objects and images. To address this issue, we propose a novel method called MCT, which leverages the strengths of both memory replay and parameter evolution strategies. MCT consists of two key components: the Memory-Enhanced Classifier (MEC) and the Object-Region Feature Evolver (ORFE). The MEC module stores and retrieves class-specific features from previous tasks, while the ORFE module dynamically updates object-related features. MCT's effectiveness is demonstrated through its ability to achieve state-of-the-art performance on challenging continual object detection benchmarks, including the Pascal VOC and COCO datasets.

Machine learning models, specifically Decision Trees (DTs) and Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), are widely used in various fields, including healthcare, due to their exceptional performance. However, the trade-off between model performance and explainability remains a significant concern. DTs are generally more transparent than DNNs, but they often struggle to achieve high performance. Conversely, DNNs can excel in complex tasks but are less interpretable. To bridge this gap, we introduce a novel method that combines the strengths of both models. Our approach involves using a decision tree to generate a set of rules, which are then utilized to generate input data for a Deep Neural Network. This allows the DNN to be trained on a more manageable dataset, ultimately improving its explainability. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method by applying it to a real-world dataset, where it outperforms traditional DT models and is comparable to the most advanced DNN models, all while being more interpretable.

The rapid growth of artificial intelligence has led to a significant increase in demand for high-performance computing resources, particularly for training and inference tasks. In response, a variety of solutions have emerged to meet this demand, including GPUs, FPGAs, and high-end CPUs. This paper compares the performance of three Intel Xeon processors with three NVIDIA GPUs, focusing on four popular deep learning frameworks: TensorFlow, PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and OpenVINO. By evaluating the performance of these models, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the capabilities of Intel Xeon processors in supporting artificial intelligence workloads. Our results demonstrate that Intel Xeon processors can efficiently execute deep learning tasks, offering a compelling alternative to traditional GPU-based solutions.

Three standard methods for determining equivalence include equivalence tests, confidence intervals, and equivalence intervals. Although these procedures are often used interchangeably, they are not equivalent to one another. This note examines the relationships between these three methods, with a focus on how confidence intervals and confidence regions can be used to derive the first two procedures.

A new approach to semantic image transmission is explored, leveraging the power of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract meaningful image features. By utilizing a CNN, the method effectively condenses complex images into lower-dimensional representations, facilitating efficient transmission over limited bandwidth channels. Furthermore, the proposed system incorporates a joint optimization framework to refine both encoding and decoding processes, ultimately enhancing image reconstruction quality. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of this novel approach in comparison to conventional compression techniques and other state-of-the-art semantic transmission systems.

In big data analytics, the ability to handle large datasets is crucial, but the current focus on processing speed has led to a lack of attention on the quality of the results. To address this issue, we introduce a new approach that balances processing efficiency with result accuracy. By incorporating result-aware techniques, the accuracy of the final output can be significantly improved without compromising performance. Our approach incorporates result-aware techniques into the MapReduce framework, incorporating them into the Map and Reduce phases. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through the implementation of result-aware MapReduce, which we call MapResultReduce, and apply it to the task of clustering. Our evaluation, which uses real-world datasets, shows that MapResultReduce can achieve better results than traditional methods while maintaining a similar processing time.

Doctrines enable categorization of various mathematical structures, specifically the Dtn 2-category, effectively captures the relationship between theories and their models. A specific type of modal interior operators can be defined within this framework, characterized by an additional doctrine. This doctrine is defined as the product of a given doctrine and the 2-category of sets. A specific morphism is then constructed within this framework, allowing for the creation of modal interior operators on any doctrine. This construction can be further exemplified by its application to the creation of modal interior operators on the Heda doctrine.

We propose a Bayesian grouped network autoregression model that allows for
identifying clusters within network data. Our approach utilizes a novel
prior, the structured stochastic block model, which is tailored to the specific
structure of our data. This model is then adapted using a modified Chinese
rocker prior to facilitate a Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling algorithm.
Our methodology is showcased through simulations and an empirical analysis of
Twitter data, which reveals the effectiveness of our method in practice.

Research is often evaluated based on the accuracy of claims made within scientific literature. However, validating these claims is a labor-intensive process that requires expert knowledge and access to relevant data. To address this challenge, we've developed an AI system that can assist researchers in verifying scientific claims by analyzing both the claim and the supporting evidence. Our system, which we term ClaimFacteR, is built on a novel framework that incorporates a multi-head attention mechanism and a specialized knowledge graph. By leveraging this architecture, we've successfully demonstrated the effectiveness of ClaimFacteR in accurately classifying the factual accuracy of claims within various scientific domains. Our results show that ClaimFacteR achieves an F1 score of 0.84 on the SCIFeVer benchmark, outperforming existing methods. Furthermore, we've developed a new dataset, SciFeVer-Enhanced, which includes an expanded set of relationships and has been used to further refine our model. Our experiments reveal that incorporating relationship types into the model significantly improves its performance, achieving an F1 score of 0.90.

This method, which is based on a deep learning architecture, has been trained using a large dataset of manually labeled images. The proposed method, which has been validated using a large dataset of 1,000 images, has shown high accuracy in identifying the key compartments of the eye. The method, which is based on a U-Net architecture, has been found to be effective in identifying the cornea, vitreous body, retina, and sclera. Cognitive models have been developed to simulate the human mind's functioning, but they often fall short in replicating the human experience of time. To address this limitation, we suggest incorporating a temporal component into these models, enabling them to track the passage of time and its impact on mental processes. This temporal dimension can be conceptualized as a fundamental aspect of reality that influences cognitive processes, and we propose a framework to model its effects on these processes. We demonstrate the practical application of this framework by applying it to a well-established cognitive model, the ACT-R, and highlight the benefits of this approach.

This study investigates the validity of several conjectures and the Eight Levels Theorem related to Mersenne primes, along-primorial numbers, and other near-prime numbers.
